metadata.title: Claude, Cookbook Audit.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude auditing a cookbook notebook is general editorial taste or something more specific, using the cookbook-audit skill's own description as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that a cookbook-audit skill is SKILL.md, a rubric Claude reads, applies, and checks the same way against whatever notebook you hand it.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (hand the skill a notebook: same three steps run every time; then the same pipeline runs identically twice, and just as readily against an issue outside the rubric)

beats.narration_text: Someone types: how do I get Claude to judge my notebook. They stop on judge — wrong verb. This skill audits against a written rubric. It doesn't have taste. Here's what that swap actually costs, and buys.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'How do I get Claude to judge my notebook?', hesitates on 'judge', corrects to 'audit', lands the real question

props.text:
How do I get Claude
to judge my notebook?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('judge' -> 'audit') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Here's what's actually happening: a skill is a folder Claude reads before it works — not weights, not training. cookbook-audit holds three files: SKILL.md, style_guide.md, and validate_notebook.py. Twelve kilobytes of plain English, no hidden logic. Claude reads the folder, then acts on what it says. The file is the program. They optimized for you being able to open it in a text editor and change it — at the expense of anything the model might do on its own.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder opening to three files, SKILL.md highlighted; 'not trained on it' callout; 'the file is the program' closer

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon opens into three file rows: SKILL.md (12k), style_guide.md (5k), and validate_notebook.py (17k) — SKILL.md recolors teal and grows slightly. A 'not trained on it' tag crosses out a brain glyph. Closing line: 'the file is the program'.

beats.narration_text: The instructions live in a Steps section: read SKILL.md, execute each step in order, return the result. Linear, no branching unless a step says so. Watch the anchor. Hand the skill a notebook, and here's what runs: it reads the rubric, checks the notebook against it, returns a score. Same three steps, every time. That's the trade — predictable mechanics on identical input, at the expense of any cleverness on input the rubric doesn't cover.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — three linear pipeline phases, then a notebook arrowing through validate_notebook.py to a rubric-score output

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — a notebook, three steps
production_viz.mechanic: Three phase cards appear left to right and connect with arrows: 'read SKILL.md' / 'execute' / 'return result'. They fade back. THE ANCHOR. A card labelled 'notebook' arrows into a card labelled 'validate_notebook.py', which arrows into a card labelled 'rubric score'. Closing line beneath: 'same three steps, every time'. THIS EXACT SEQUENCE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Here's the payoff. Same notebook, same score, every run — hand cookbook-audit the identical notebook twice and you get identical rubric scores both times. That's what a file-as-program buys you. The reverse holds too: a notebook with an issue outside the stated rubric still runs the same three steps, checking only what SKILL.md names. validate_notebook.py is the check on the check — right structure, right rubric items, right scope, all caught the same way. They optimized for auditability. If you wanted a general reviewer that catches surprises, that's a different tool.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same pipeline firing identically twice, then split: identical notebook twice = identical score; issue outside rubric = same steps still run, both checked by validate_notebook.py

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same input, same output; then the limit
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 PIPELINE RETURNS, identical, running twice in a row — two matching 'rubric score' cards appear side by side, labelled 'same input, same output'. Then it splits: left card 'in-rubric notebook' → pipeline → clean score, labelled 'the payoff'; right card 'out-of-rubric issue' → the same pipeline → score returned anyway, labelled 'the limit'. Beneath both, a small 'validate_notebook.py' tag with a check and a cross — right structure, right rubric items, right scope. Closing line: 'only what SKILL.md names'.

beats.narration_text: Auditing a cookbook notebook isn't Claude forming its own opinion of quality — it's SKILL.md, a rubric Claude reads, applies, and checks the same way against whatever notebook you hand it.
